title: Choir and Portrait
premise: Ansel Montrose, a hospice nurse who records the dying counting backwards, discovers the count is an invocation: each death at Blackthorn House has fed something the family invited in generations ago. When the mirrors begin lagging a second behind reality, Ansel realizes he has been chosen as the final voice in the choir. To survive until sunrise, he must choose between completing his documentation — which would seal the entity's power forever — and burning it, freeing the trapped dead but erasing every soul it holds, including the woman he loves. He burns the archive at dawn, and the house forgets him; only his own handwriting on his skin remains as proof.
about_author: Sable Nakamura is a former night-shift caregiver who writes horror about institutions, grief, and the paperwork of dying. They live near the coast with too many clocks and one very old mirror.

chapters.title: The Count
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. On his first week at Blackthorn House hospice, patient Edith Vane counts down from ninety-one and dies exactly at zero. Ansel documents it obsessively, noting three other charts with identical patterns. The emotional beat is quiet professional unease curdling into obsession — documentation as prayer, prayer as compulsion.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. His own reflection blinks after he does. Testing every mirror in the house, he finds the lag growing — half a second, then a full second — and in the delayed image, the hallway behind him holds figures that aren't there. Beat: dread arriving through the most mundane medium.

chapters.title: The Family That Invited
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, intercut with 1899 letters from patriarch Aldous Vane. The letters reveal a bargain: the family traded their deaths to something they called the Choirmaster, feeding it the last breaths of others to postpone their own. Beat: the horror of inherited debt and the corruption of purchased power.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Mara Vane, the last living heir, arrives to sign her grandmother into care — and Ansel recognizes her voice from the mirrors. She hears nothing, sees nothing, but she hums the countdown melody in her sleep. Falling for her feels like treason against his own survival instinct. Beat: love against duty begins.

chapters.title: Chorus of the Dying
chapters.summary: Multiple POV via Ansel's recordings. Three patients begin counting simultaneously, voices harmonizing, and the house's clocks all stop at 3:33. Ansel plays back his tapes and hears a fourth voice beneath his own narration, answering questions he never asked aloud. Beat: the investigation becomes a conversation with the predator.

chapters.title: What the Mirrors Keep
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. He enters the sealed conservatory where the original contract was signed and finds the mirrors there reflect not the room but the moment of invitation, replaying endlessly. The Choirmaster speaks through Aldous's preserved face: Ansel was hired because his documenting habit makes him the perfect vessel. Beat: the trap revealed — his devotion weaponized.

chapters.title: Zero Hour
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Mara's grandmother dies at midnight and the count doesn't stop — it transfers to Mara, now counting down from sunrise. Ansel confesses everything; Mara, furious and terrified, chooses to stay and fight rather than flee, insisting any justice must include burning the family name. Beat: love and duty finally aligned.

chapters.title: The Vigil
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Through the small hours, the entity strips away exits, staff, and electricity, offering Ansel immortality in exchange for finishing his archive — the completed record would bind the dead permanently to the house. Each refusal costs him a memory. Beat: power's temptation staged as mercy.

chapters.title: Sunrise Clause
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, climax. At zero, the Choirmaster comes for Mara, and Ansel realizes the archive itself is the contract's anchor. He sets fire to forty years of his documentation in the conservatory as the mirrors shatter inward, screaming in harmony. Beat: justice outside the law, paid for in his own recorded past.

chapters.title: Afterimage
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, resolution. The house stands empty and ordinary; no records of Ansel exist anywhere except words inked across her forearm in handwriting she somehow knows. She finds one unburned page — his first entry, Edith's count — and understands what he paid. Beat: grief, proof, and love surviving erasure.
